title: Mason the Mail Carrier
lines: Hi there. Come on in. Mind the easel.
I thought today we’d paint a happy little mail carrier.
I’ve already covered the canvas with a thin, even coat of Liquid Gravel.
Warm colours today. Just let the sky glow.
The sun sets every day, and nobody claps. Let’s clap. ...Quietly.
A big mesa. That’s Spanish for table. So it’s a rock, for table.
These are the tall cousins. We don’t see them much.
Desert floor. Warm and dry. Rocks do very well out here.
Nobody waters us. We’re fine.
Time to wash the brush.
And then you just...
(heh heh) It’s the only violence on this programme.
Now then. Let’s have some fun.
Let’s put a pebble in this world.
Start with his shadow. The shadow always arrives first. It’s very keen.
Feet. Pebbles have feet. Please don’t write in.
Take some Alizarin Crimson. Load the brush full.
Just a happy little blob. He’s a river rock.
A shadow side, and a little light on top. Now he’s round. A second ago he was a sticker.
He needs a job. In this economy, even pebbles work.
He delivers the mail. Slowly. He’s a pebble.
And two little arms. Just let them flop.
Let’s give him an afro. I’m not biased.
A little cap. Very official.
Two little dots. And now he can see you. Say hello.
Give him a letter. Careful, now. No fingers.
And a signature. Moss. That’s me.
And I think we’ll call that one finished. That’s Mason.
Thank you for watching. Happy pebbling, and rock bless, my friend.

title: Pearl the Rock Star
lines: Hi there. Come on in. Mind the easel.
I have a real treat for you today. A rock star. And he’s a pebble.
I’ve already covered the canvas with a thin, even coat of Liquid Gravel.
A little Phthalo Blue for the sky. Just dance it in.
Clouds are very free. They float around all day. A pebble can’t relate.
A big wave. Let it crash. It worked hard to get here.
The sea is where pebbles come from. This is basically a baby picture.
Wet sand. Pull across, and let it shine.
A beach is ten million pebbles who all get along.
Time to wash the brush.
And then you just...
(heh heh) It’s the only violence on this programme.
Now then. Let’s have some fun.
Let’s put a pebble in this world.
Start with his shadow. The shadow always arrives first. It’s very keen.
Feet. Pebbles have feet. Please don’t write in.
Indian Yellow. Drop him right in, top to bottom.
There’s no wrong way to make a pebble. The river’s been guessing for years.
A shadow side, and a little light on top. Now he’s round. A second ago he was a sticker.
Oop. Dropped a little paint there.
That’s alright. We don’t make mistakes here. Just happy little sediments.
Now let’s get him dressed for work.
He’s a rock star. He plays rock. I don’t know what you expected.
Arms. I like to give them arms. Mine came this way.
Just let it fall. Long hair. He’s in a band, but only on weekends.
Two little dots. And now he can see you. Say hello.
Sunglasses. Indoors. He’s that kind of pebble.
And he’ll need a guitar.
Remember our happy little accident?
He’s a pebble now. Everybody needs a friend.
And a signature. Moss. That’s me.
And I think we’ll call that one finished. That’s Pearl.
Until next time. Happy pebbling, and rock bless.

title: Stoney the Ballerina
lines: Welcome back. Is it that time already? Good.
I thought today we’d paint a happy little ballerina.
I’ve already covered the canvas with a thin, even coat of Liquid Gravel.
A little Phthalo Blue for the sky. Just dance it in.
Clouds are very free. They float around all day. A pebble can’t relate.
Now the knife. A big strong mountain. Just pull it down the side.
A mountain is only a pebble that believed in itself.
A little lake. Pebbles love a lake.
We go in. We sink. We stay. It’s a lifestyle.
And some ground, so our friend has somewhere to stand.
That’s important. Everybody needs somewhere to stand.
Time to wash the brush.
And then you just...
(heh heh) It’s the only violence on this programme.
Now for the reason we all came.
A pebble. With a job.
Start with his shadow. The shadow always arrives first. It’s very keen.
Feet. Pebbles have feet. Please don’t write in.
Take some Phthalo Blue. Load the brush full.
There’s no wrong way to make a pebble. The river’s been guessing for years.
A shadow side, and a little light on top. Now he’s round. A second ago he was a sticker.
He needs a job. In this economy, even pebbles work.
A ballerina. Very graceful, for a rock.
Arms. I like to give them arms. Mine came this way.
A neat side part. He reads the evening news, on channel four.
A tiny tiara. She earned it.
Two little dots. And now he can see you. Say hello.
Give him a little sparkle. Careful, now. No fingers.
And a signature. Moss. That’s me.
And I think we’ll call that one finished. That’s Stoney.
Thank you for watching. Happy pebbling, and rock bless, my friend.
